mainEntity.name: Will a new roof increase my home’s value or help if I plan to sell soon?

acceptedAnswer.text:
A **new roof often boosts curb appeal, reduces buyer objections, and can improve resale value**, especially if the old roof is visibly aged or leaking. It may not return every dollar in a quick flip, but it can make your home easier and faster to sell.

Buyers and inspectors pay close attention to roof condition because replacement is a major expense. An old or questionable roof often leads to price negotiations or delayed closings.

Key factors:
- Age and appearance of your current roof
- Local buyer expectations and competition
- Transferability of warranties to the new owner
- Energy-efficient or cool-roof upgrades you install

If you plan to sell within a few years, talk with your agent and roofer about what level of roof work makes the most sense—full replacement, targeted repairs, or a documented professional inspection. Being able to show a recent roof report and clear documentation reassures buyers and strengthens your negotiating position.
